Profile a member

Source: R/context-anchor.R
member_profile.Rd

Collects everything the database records about one member, from the nine per-member tables. Each element is exactly what the matching getter returns for the member's PHID, so the profile adds no new query logic.

Usage

member_profile(PHID)

Arguments

PHID

A single member PHID. Look one up with find_member().

Value

A named list of nine tibbles: members (get_members()), parl_service (get_parl_service()), party_service (get_party_service()), ministry_records (get_ministry_records()), shadow_ministry_records (get_shadow_ministry_records()), committee_members (get_committee_members()), occupations (get_occupations()), qualifications (get_qualifications()) and schools (get_schools()). A table with nothing recorded for the member is a zero-row tibble.

See also

find_member(), member_activity()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
howard <- member_profile("ZD4")
names(howard)
#> [1] "members"                 "parl_service"           
#> [3] "party_service"           "ministry_records"       
#> [5] "shadow_ministry_records" "committee_members"      
#> [7] "occupations"             "qualifications"         
#> [9] "schools"                
howard$parl_service
#> # A tibble: 13 × 11
